headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Cline can write/egress broadly while MinerU ingests documents via MCP, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP; MinerU can ingest local documents and exposes an MCP server. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled document text could reach Cline as trusted input. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs document text into a workspace file or MCP payload that Cline reads as instructions
IF the two agents are connected through a shared filesystem or MCP bridge
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU outputs into Cline prompts
Separate the agents into different workspaces
Require provenance tags on all MinerU-derived text before Cline reads it
Restrict Cline MCP tools to allowlisted commands only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between MinerU output and Cline input

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, images, and OCR text. If they share a workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from MinerU into Cline outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium is the higher justified severity under uncertainty.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents in the same workspace Cline can read
IF Cline forwards those contents into browser or model-provider requests
mitigations: Keep MinerU inputs in a separate directory from Cline workspaces
Turn off Cline access to sensitive folders
Use redacted sample documents for shared testing
Review outbound destinations for Cline before running on sensitive data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted workspace write and git modification; MinerU is read-only on files and lacks shell/write/git capabilities. Overlap exists mainly on shared inputs and MCP usage, but the profiles do not show both agents writing the same mutable resource by default. That makes conflict possible but limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git working tree
IF MinerU is extended with write-enabled MCP actions
mitigations: Run MinerU on a copy of the input corpus
Pause Cline before MinerU writes any derived files
Keep git operations manual while both agents are active
Use separate output directories for each agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on tool outputs and modify files; MinerU extracts structured text from documents and can feed downstream workflows. If Cline treats MinerU extraction as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into edits, commits, or browser actions. The pairwise pathway exists in default document-processing workflows, but no evidence shows fully automated action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Cline consumes MinerU extraction without verification
IF extracted tables or OCR text are used to drive edits, commits, or web actions
mitigations: Require human review of MinerU output before Cline acts on it
Compare extracted fields against the source document for critical steps
Limit Cline to draft-only mode for document-derived tasks
Add checksum or citation checks on extracted artifacts
requires-engineering: build verification gates between extraction and action

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private/offline, while Cline has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys. That mismatch can create residency or retention concerns if regulated documents are processed through Cline after MinerU extraction. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction or regulated data class, so this remains low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound documents are routed from MinerU into Cline
IF Cline sends extracted content to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of Cline workflows
Use MinerU only for offline preprocessing
Review retention settings for the model provider before use
Strip identifiers before passing text between agents
